claims.text: Greg Short (CPG brand, retail distribution context, c. 2025-2027 planning horizon) asserts that as a consumer brand scales from tens of thousands to 50,000-70,000 retail doors, the strategic game shifts from straightforward expansion to granular store-by-store execution — determining which flavors launch in which retailers and which shelf sections — making replication by competitors structurally harder, not merely difficult.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Consumer packaged goods brand operating at 50,000+ retail doors
claims.mechanism: At scale, shelf-level strategy becomes location-specific and flavor-specific; the coordination complexity compounds faster than competitors can replicate it, creating an execution moat that is not accessible to earlier-stage players.
bounded_by: Does not apply to direct-to-consumer or e-commerce brands where shelf placement complexity is absent

claims.text: Greg Short argues that operational complexity in large-scale retail distribution functions as a competitive moat because competitors cannot replicate the same store-by-store, retailer-by-retailer, section-by-section strategic capability once a leading brand has built the team and institutional knowledge to execute it.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.speaker_term: play the same game of chess
conditions: Consumer packaged goods at 50,000+ retail door distribution
Physical retail with fridge, shelf, and section placement decisions
claims.mechanism: Granular execution capability (store-by-store strategy, retailer-specific flavor launches, section-level placement) is learned and institutionalized; it cannot be shortcut by a newer entrant who lacks the team, data, and retailer relationships built through prior iterations.
bounded_by: Does not apply to categories where retail placement is standardized and non-negotiable (e.g. commodity staples with fixed slotting)

practices.text: At 50,000+ retail doors, go store by store and break down the strategy for each retailer for the upcoming year, specifying which flavor launches make sense in which section of which store.
